title: Connectivity & Quality
description: Is the connection's quality changing, and when? Loss and latency by kind of destination on one time axis, the episodes the inference module detected, and loss by day and hour of day.

links.title: Target detail
links.tooltip: Every layer measured for one target

panels.title: The selected range at a glance
Mean loss, destinations
panels.description: Share of pings lost across every destination over the selected range. The ISP gateway (rate-limited, with a loss floor of its own) and the DNS wizard's targets are left out.

targets.query: from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:v.timeRangeStart, stop:v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn:(r) => r._measurement == "latency" and r._field == "loss" and r.category != "dns_wizard" and r.category != "cpe") |> group() |> mean()

panels.title: Probe cycles with loss on 2+ destinations
panels.description: Share of 5-minute probe cycles in which at least two destinations lost packets at once. One destination losing is that destination; two or more together point at the house, the line or the ISP.

targets.query: from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:v.timeRangeStart, stop:v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn:(r) => r._measurement == "latency" and r._field == "loss" and r.category != "dns_wizard" and r.category != "cpe") |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: max, createEmpty: false, timeSrc: "_start") |> map(fn:(r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: if r._value > 0.0 then 1 else 0})) |> group() |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: sum, createEmpty: false, timeSrc: "_start") |> map(fn:(r) => ({r with _value: if r._value >= 2 then 1.0 else 0.0})) |> mean()

panels.title: Loss degradation periods (experimental)
panels.description: Periods the inference module found where a destination's loss rose and stayed (Bayesian change points on 15-minute loss) that overlap the range; the ISP gateway and the DNS wizard's targets are left out. Empty when the inference profile is off: `smoking-pi enable inference`. Periods in which the monitor itself was deaf are not counted.

targets.query:
import "date"
from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start: date.sub(d: 14d, from: v.timeRangeStart), stop: v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn:(r) => r._measurement == "loss_degradation" and (r._field == "end" or r._field == "class") and r.category != "cpe" and r.category != "dns_wizard") |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time", "target"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value") |> filter(fn: (r) => r.end * 1000000000 >= int(v: v.timeRangeStart)) |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.class or r.class != "monitor_deaf") |> group() |> count(column: "end")

panels.title: Persistent congestion periods (experimental)
panels.description: Periods Jitterbug (as published: change points on the minimum RTT, then the latency jump and a KS test) labeled congested on a destination, that overlap the range. Empty when the inference profile is off: `smoking-pi enable inference`.

targets.query:
import "date"
from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start: date.sub(d: 14d, from: v.timeRangeStart), stop: v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn:(r) => r._measurement == "persistent_congestion" and r._field == "end" and r.category != "cpe" and r.category != "dns_wizard") |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time", "target"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value") |> filter(fn: (r) => r.end * 1000000000 >= int(v: v.timeRangeStart)) |> group() |> count(column: "end")

panels.title: Over the selected range, on one time axis
ICMP loss by category, mean across targets (0–10 %)
panels.description: The Overview's loss panel zoomed to 0–10 %, where everyday loss lives; a cut above 10 % runs off the top, and a red dot on the top edge marks each window where a category did; hover it for the real value (the Overview shows the full scale). Several categories rising together is the link; one alone is its destinations. The ISP gateway rate-limits ICMP, so its line sits on a floor of its own. Click a line to open that category's targets side by side over the same range.

from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:v.timeRangeStart, stop:v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn:(r) => r._measurement == "latency" and r._field == "loss" and r.category != "dns_wizard") |> group(columns:["category"]) |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false) |> filter(fn:(r) => r._value > 0.1) |> keep(columns:["_time","_value"]) |> group() |> unique(column:"_time") |> map(fn:(r) => ({r with _value: 0.1})) |> set(key:"_field", value:"above") |> sort(columns:["_time"])

panels.title: ICMP latency by category, median across targets
panels.description: The median of every target's median ping in each window, per category. A step in one line is that kind of destination; a step in all of them is the house or the ISP. The ISP gateway is left out: it answers ICMP from its control plane, whose spikes of hundreds of milliseconds would flatten every other line (the Overview charts it toward the ISP). Click a line to open that category's targets side by side over the same range.

value.title: The resolvers side by side, same range

targets.query: from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:v.timeRangeStart, stop:v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn:(r) => r._measurement == "latency" and r._field == "median" and r.category != "dns_wizard" and r.category != "cpe") |> group(columns:["category"]) |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: median, createEmpty: false) |> map(fn:(r) => ({r with name: if r.category == "topsites" then "Top sites" else if r.category == "netflix" then "Netflix OCA" else if r.category == "dns" then "DNS resolvers" else if r.category == "custom" then "Custom" else if r.category == "cpe" then "ISP gateway" else if r.category == "unknown" then "Uncategorized" else r.category})) |> drop(columns:["_start","_stop"]) |> group(columns:["category","name"]) |> sort(columns:["_time"])

panels.title: Detected episodes, by target (experimental)
panels.description: What the inference module found, on the same time axis: red is loss degradation, orange is persistent congestion (Jitterbug). Every target the module analyzes, the ISP gateway included: its rows say whether the first hop moved too. Detected, not confirmed: compare with the loss and latency above. Empty when the inference profile is off. Gray: the monitor itself was deaf for most of the period (its radio heard nothing), so the loss is this Pi's, not the destination's. Click a bar for every layer of that target over the same range, with the period shaded.

targets.query:
import "date"
// A period is stamped at its start: reach back so one that began before
// the range but ends inside it is still drawn.
// class is "monitor_deaf" when this Pi's radio heard nothing for most of the period (deaf.py); periods written before the class existed are loss.
degradations = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: date.sub(d: 14d, from: v.timeRangeStart), stop: v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "loss_degradation" and (r._field == "end" or r._field == "class")) |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time", "target"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value") |> filter(fn: (r) => r.end * 1000000000 >= int(v: v.timeRangeStart))
loss_degradation = degradations |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r.class or r.class != "monitor_deaf") |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, target: r.target, kind: "loss degradation", end: time(v: r.end * 1000000000)}))
monitor_deaf = degradations |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.class and r.class == "monitor_deaf") |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, target: r.target, kind: "monitor deaf", end: time(v: r.end * 1000000000)}))
persistent_congestion = from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: date.sub(d: 14d, from: v.timeRangeStart), stop: v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "persistent_congestion" and r._field == "end") |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time", "target"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value") |> filter(fn: (r) => r.end * 1000000000 >= int(v: v.timeRangeStart)) |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, target: r.target, kind: "persistent congestion", end: time(v: r.end * 1000000000)}))
starts = union(tables: [
    loss_degradation |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, target: r.target, kind: r.kind, _value: 1})),
    persistent_congestion |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, target: r.target, kind: r.kind, _value: 2})),
    monitor_deaf |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, target: r.target, kind: r.kind, _value: 3})),
])
ends = union(tables: [loss_degradation, persistent_congestion, monitor_deaf]) |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r.end, target: r.target, kind: r.kind, _value: 0}))
union(tables: [starts, ends]) |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _time: if r._time < v.timeRangeStart then v.timeRangeStart else r._time})) |> group(columns: ["target", "kind"]) |> sort(columns: ["_time", "_value"])

panels.title: Inference passes (experimental): seconds per hourly pass, failures
panels.description: One point per pass of the inference service: how long the pass took for all its targets, and how many targets failed. The record the service keeps of itself (status.json holds only the last pass).

targets.query: from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "inference_pass" and (r._field == "seconds" or r._field == "errors")) |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_field", "_value"])

panels.title: The targets behind the loss, over the selected range
Targets behind the loss, most loss first
panels.description: Every destination that lost packets in the selected range: the share of its pings lost, the probe cycles in which it lost at least one, and its worst cycle. Several targets of one category at the top is that category; the same share on every target is the link. Click a target for every layer of it on one page or for its individual pings, a category for its targets side by side. The ISP gateway and the DNS wizard's targets are left out, as in the tiles.

value.title: Every target of this category, same range

targets.query:
base = from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:v.timeRangeStart, stop:v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn:(r) => r._measurement == "latency" and r._field == "loss" and r.category != "dns_wizard" and r.category != "cpe")
// Three bare aggregates per target, each answered in the storage engine; the join is a pivot over a few hundred rows.
mean = base |> mean() |> set(key:"_field", value:"mean") |> keep(columns:["target","category","_field","_value"])
worst = base |> max() |> set(key:"_field", value:"worst") |> keep(columns:["target","category","_field","_value"])
lossy = base |> filter(fn:(r) => r._value > 0.0) |> count() |> toFloat() |> set(key:"_field", value:"lossy") |> keep(columns:["target","category","_field","_value"])
union(tables:[mean, worst, lossy]) |> group() |> pivot(rowKey:["target","category"], columnKey:["_field"], valueColumn:"_value") |> filter(fn:(r) => r.mean > 0.0) |> sort(columns:["mean"], desc:true)

panels.title: When does it happen? (last 30 days, local time)
Mean loss across destinations, day × hour
panels.description: Each cell is one hour of one day: the mean share of pings lost across every destination (the ISP gateway and the DNS wizard's targets left out). A recurring evening band is a daily pattern; a single bright cell is one event.

targets.query:
import "timezone"
import "date"
tz = "${__timezone}"
loc = timezone.location(name: if tz == "utc" or tz == "" or tz == "browser" then "UTC" else tz)
from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:v.timeRangeStart, stop:v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn:(r) => r._measurement == "latency" and r._field == "loss" and r.category != "dns_wizard" and r.category != "cpe") |> group() |> aggregateWindow(every: 1h, fn: mean, createEmpty: false, location: loc, timeSrc: "_start") |> map(fn:(r) => ({_time: date.truncate(t: r._time, unit: 1d, location: loc), hour: (if date.hour(t: r._time, location: loc) < 10 then "0" else "") + string(v: date.hour(t: r._time, location: loc)), _value: r._value})) |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["hour"], valueColumn: "_value") |> sort(columns: ["_time"])

panels.title: Probe cycles with loss on 2+ destinations, day × hour
panels.description: Each cell is one hour of one day: the share of its probe cycles in which at least two destinations lost packets at once. Less sensitive to a single long cut than the mean, and the clearest signal of loss the destinations share.

targets.query:
import "timezone"
import "date"
tz = "${__timezone}"
loc = timezone.location(name: if tz == "utc" or tz == "" or tz == "browser" then "UTC" else tz)
from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:v.timeRangeStart, stop:v.timeRangeStop) |> filter(fn:(r) => r._measurement == "latency" and r._field == "loss" and r.category != "dns_wizard" and r.category != "cpe") |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: max, createEmpty: false, timeSrc: "_start") |> map(fn:(r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: if r._value > 0.0 then 1 else 0})) |> group() |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: sum, createEmpty: false, timeSrc: "_start") |> map(fn:(r) => ({r with _value: if r._value >= 2 then 1.0 else 0.0})) |> group() |> aggregateWindow(every: 1h, fn: mean, createEmpty: false, location: loc, timeSrc: "_start") |> map(fn:(r) => ({_time: date.truncate(t: r._time, unit: 1d, location: loc), hour: (if date.hour(t: r._time, location: loc) < 10 then "0" else "") + string(v: date.hour(t: r._time, location: loc)), _value: r._value})) |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["hour"], valueColumn: "_value") |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
